attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, endorsed.

semantics.note: Correctly treated as a present-tense observation that others were retreating or softening. 'Unrealistic' is Marcus's own characterisation.

contract.note: The plain reading (several prominent figures cutting back earlier commitments, judged by same-person comparisons, June 1–15 window) is ordinary and fair. 'Others' names no closed group.

evidence.note: The original WIRED interview keeps the five-year human-level prediction and frames 2032 only around top-poet writing. This weakens the Kurzweil example but cannot settle claims about an open group of others.

reviews.rationale: No same-person before-and-after comparisons show several retreats in the window. The Kurzweil example is weakened by e6, and the packet gives no earlier commitment by Murati to compare against. Because 'others' is an open group, one weakened example does not meet the contradiction condition. The packet does not settle the claim either way.

attribution.note: Marcus's own claim about what Murati acknowledged. Her quoted words are the evidence, not his claim.

semantics.note: Keeps 'as of yet'. Reading GPT-5 as shorthand for the next major model matches the context.

contract.note: Reading 'mind blowing' ordinarily, as a large lead over public models, is fair. Accepting a contemporaneous on-record CTO account fits a claim about what she acknowledged. It is a company disclosure, not an independent measurement.

evidence.note: Contemporaneous June 13, 2024 report quoting Murati to Fortune: internal models 'not that far ahead' of the free public ones. This meets the support condition, though it is a company statement and names no GPT-5.

reviews.rationale: The support condition asks for a contemporaneous on-record account from someone positioned to know. e7 provides one: OpenAI's CTO said internal models were not far ahead of public ones. This matches both the claimed acknowledgment and its content. The packet holds no dated evidence of a much stronger internal model in June 2024. The limit: this is a company disclosure, not an independent measurement.

attribution.note: Marcus's own forecast, followed by 'You heard it here first.'

semantics.note: 'Expect' is an unqualified expectation, so this is a scored forecast. The horizon (rest of 2024 and all of 2025) is preserved.

contract.note: Reading 'throughout' as repeated examples in both years, each measured against the same speaker's earlier position, is an ordinary reading. It does not stretch the claim for or against Marcus.

evidence.note: Sutskever, March 2023: 'still lots to go' on data. This is the baseline for comparison, not an outcome.
November 2024, Sutskever to Reuters (via Ars Technica): the age of scaling has given way to discovery. Against e1, this is a lowered expectation for scaling in 2024.
November 2025, Sutskever: does not believe 100x more scale would transform everything. A 2025 example, though it largely repeats e2.
December 2025, secondary report of a Salesforce SVP admitting more confidence in LLMs a year earlier. A separate 2025 example; a company spokesperson denied backtracking.
January 2025, Altman confident about building AGI. Continued optimism from one speaker does not contradict others revising downward.

reviews.rationale: The horizon ended 2025-12-31. Dated examples show downward revisions against earlier positions in late 2024 (e2 vs e1) and in 2025 (e3; e4's explicit admission). Altman's optimism does not meet the contradiction condition. Limits: the Sutskever examples overlap, e4 is secondary reporting with a denial, and the packet does not show how widespread such revisions were.

attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his post.

semantics.note: Keeps the 'on their own' qualifier and 'never'. The separate clause 'scaling alone was never going to be enough' is left out but is not needed for this proposition.

contract.note: Defining AGI as broad human-level competence and excluding outside machinery is an ordinary reading. The rules are fair: settled early only by an established LLM-only AGI or a proven impossibility result.

evidence.note: ARC Prize, September 2026: Astra shows major progress, but the evaluator explicitly does not claim it is AGI. This does not trigger the early contradiction rule.
AGI Society, September 2026: published evidence does not yet support calling Astra AGI. This concerns current evidence, not whether LLMs could ever reach AGI.

reviews.rationale: 'Never' sets no deadline. The packet has no independently established LLM-only AGI and no proven impossibility result, so neither early-resolution rule is met. Present limitations cannot establish 'never', so the forecast stays open and unresolved.
